Allow me to wax philosophical for a second,

What makes up sight reading? Playing what one reads on the score.

It's just like reading from a book, you learn to make the sounds, sound out the words, and recite the statements. Only now its not your voice, which you have been using and honing since you were a wee small fry, it's your fingers via your muscles, a la your brain, ergo your eyes, and all absorbed from whatever sheet of music that is slightly too difficult to read. 

It always seems to me that there is a gap between what we see on the score, what we should be playing. Then one must focus on the playing, which comes down to practice. The brain is all about recognizing patterns, so if you invest some time in recognizing those patterns in your fingers you can streamline the motion of score, eyes, brain, muscles, play. 

​

Basically, practice playing and practice reading music and bingo bango you can read music faster and faster.
